Nice trade, Doc

I have a logic question about pro money, hope you can leave me some clues.

We know most of your trades belong to breakout retest, and those retest trades are highly successful and logic. Since retest trade is more safer and certain than breakout trade, why don't pro money trade like you do? Why a pro money doesn't wait for, lets say other pro money to reverse the trend firstly, then this pro money enter when there's a retest occur?

I can think out two reasons: 1) pro money has huge amount of capital, their orders can not get fully filled at retest price level 2) retest price level is less profitable to them

In other words, my question can be: WIll you trade the same way(trade retest) if you manage $10 billions dollar account? Will your trades become easier(can influence market) or harder(no enough retail orders to fill your orders)? Will you maintain the same % return? Because we all know the top hedge funds averagely achieve under 30% return per year.:)

Thank you!

PivO wrote:

Doctor wrote: Here is why Box A are sellers and Box B are buyers.

When you enter the market in Box A, you 'buy' into the market. You do not make any money until you close your position in profit, and profits are not gained unless there is a willing buyer of your position when you close it. He buys from you, (price is still going up) but your position is sold to him, therefore its a sell.......

Post#24, #70, #72:)

Doctor wrote: Hi PivO,

Can you show the post number so I can read the context of my words. I will comment further then.

It is in post #69. I read the posts following it. I would like to know whether lack of supply (box A) or lack of demand (box B) has a meaning in the movement.

Thanks.

PivO,

The explanation behind box A and B has already been given, but here is a brief reply on it. When you enter the market long, you are doing so with the intention of selling to the herd i.e retail trader. When you enter the market short, you are doing so with the intention of buying coming from the retail trader when you close the position. We know both instances to be true because the majority of retail traders fail and burn up accounts quickly.

As price moves the last thing you want to do is chase it, let it settle back into a pull back and then enter when the pull back has completed. This is the safest and lowest risk way you can trade. It is vital you develop your brain so it thinks before you enter the market and ask a few logical questions as part of the process. Who am I entering with?....unless the answer is pro money, you do not take the trade. You also ask where is my target and if you can find a place where its probable for pro money to push into strongly thus pulling in the herd for the last time, then this is a good place to exit.

There are opposing forces at work and it will be hard to retrain your brain into thinking on both sides of a trade before you take it. When you buy, you have to think as selling to the herd and as a seller you need to think as a buyer from the herd. It is two schools of logic and become grounded in each. Does all this make sense to you?

blacky,

pro money has the only ability to move the market, a lot of liquid money. Only liquidity moves the market and if all of us here were to put all our life savings into the market it would not move it. Pro money are the market makers and only for them there would be no market. You need a lot of money to get an instrument to move and once momentum is behind it the pro money guys can sit back and watch the herd come in and let the free market forces take over. When this happens people call it a trending market with higher highs and high lows etc. The only time pro money will get out and back in after the initial push is on pull backs, but in order for that to happen pro money has to stop a move in the opposite direction from happening which means they trade against themselves for a while. This dead money is vital to get clawed back because missing targets by even a few points is major money lost to them. A single point can be worth tens of millions, or more. These guys dont trade standard lots.

There are a few models used by pro money, one is a private fund where big finance houses trade with their own money. They are free to place trades at prices they are interested in and get out at prices also chosen by them. Others trading firms have investor funds arrive daily and they are told which instrument to trade, what price to get in and what price to get out. The trading firms get commission for trading the funds regardless of win or loose. The latter business is pure cut throat and the traders are under severe pressure to perform and they have lousy hit rate, 50% would be considered good for them.

If I had a 10 billion dollar account (back transfer only please:) ) and have free reign to trade as I please I would trade no differently than I do now. My hit rate is far in excess of the day trading houses and my return on a weekly basis far in excess of the annual hedge fund returns. I see no reason to change what works for me. As for the 10 billion effect on the market, it may make a spike on the 1 and 5 min chart. On higher time frames it will have the same effect as a screen door keeping water out of a submarine.

If I wanted market influence I then become a market maker and putting a large sum of money into the market in one hit is a major mistake. It is best to filter it in and filter it back out so you dont cause influence. Keeping the order that we have now is how money is made, and in vast sums. The 10 billion on offer is tiny when you consider the daily sum traded in forex is 4000 billion.

Many times I mention higher time frames and these are the best to trade off. But can you imagine the pressure put on a day trader in London or NY to get clients money to work in the market even though we may be hours or days away from a higher time potential turn where the best profit can be made. Thats a disadvantage they have and one I can sit and wait while price works itself out, then enter at the right time and let price action guide me because I know pro money will still be active at the most logical place where price should turn. But I didnt loose client money while waiting for the higher time frame to unwind.

Hey Dr.

Do you care to share some thoughts on the SPY? I have been watching the price action on the daily and weekly. I would expect for price to turn and go back up from one of the two yellow arrows. The problem is that most of the time I wait for PA on lower charts, price never pulls back for an opportunity! Then I end up missing a large part of the move if not all of it.

Hey H,

It is difficult to try and winkle out a days profit on a 5 min chart. Of course logic states the 5min will turn before the daily time frame, but the turn is only valid when the daily is in an area of demand. Look at todays price action (daily chart) and you will see a lot of buying, even though lower time frames dont show as clean a picture. At present only the 5min has a lot of buying activity and its previous and most recent supply was broken through and closed above. Early signs of bullish activity, yes, but far too early unless you have deep pockets.

It is better to see a base being built and tested before we push higher. Pro money will only take this in a bullish direction if there is good reason to do so. Given we have had a long bullish move up and now a 5% average correction, you have to ask is this enough?....the question and answer may be unfair because it is a pro money problem you are trying to solve.

There is something to be gained from weighting up a bullish move, is there room for profit and an obvious target?.....we know there are sellers higher up and for price to fall it will first ideally go back to the source of the move down we just had. Price action on the way down on lower time trames took most of the pro money with it in very fast order. The reason is there was a target they wanted to reach and quickly. To get above current price action there are some sellers which have to be absorbed before we see others get involved.

It is now very close to the NY close and not worth taking a risk, better to sit, watch and wait for a better entry. My thoughts are still that it is early bullish sentiment coming in after the big shake out.

Do not be concerned if you miss an entry on any time frame under the 4hr. They come around pretty often during an average week and once taken off a good area they can pull in a good few % on an account. I have noted on the S&P that pushing outside of defined areas is common place and so too are false moves. It is not as clean as major forex pairs.

I was just asking as I have tried to do this with my long term money in my 401K. For that I don't look at lower time frames, I generally look at daily and above. It just seems that with the trend the S&P can put on I often end up missing much of the move once it gets going.
H, if a daily entry is causing you to miss much of a move, it suggests you really want to trade off lower time frames.

While the media was brain washing everyone into thinking the Euro is in its death throws, pro money was loading up long based on the daily and higher time frames. If you look at the nice false bearish break and subsequent failure, it was bound to be entertainment for the bulls. What surprised me was the sheer scale of the bullish move, the time it took, and the time in which it had taken place. We are heading for the NY close and those who were short were taken out, and those who shorted off supply in lower time frames were also taken out.

I had a scaled in position as I usually tend to do on higher time frames and with the price action continuing to push strong I put on more as time moved on. There was a combined 4500+ points profit as I closed out when I took this screen shot. 10% of that would have been a nice week these days on a single pair, but taking what was on offer and not waiting for more was the prudent thing to do.

At present the euro winding up again and I see lots of pro money bullish activity and well hidden from view. They are likely now to gun for the old top back in June and then take a breather above that where price will come back and settle down for a while. At least, that is what I would prefer to see happen because we then have a clear direction with pro bears well and truly removed from the market.
Doc... the one and only! Very nice, thanks for sharring Doc

You are welcome Mel.

I hope the continuation will provide plenty profit for all. All you have to do for now is look at how price is settling down and accepting current levels. The common perception of price action of wick/tail candles off supply/demand or support/resistance is not the full picture of where contracts are coming into the market. But try as I may, it is very difficult to show where more subtle signs of pro money activity lay. It is more spread out over time and money comes in on small waves of buying or selling prior to the move. It wont show up on many candles and the market will look very much subdued.

The best I can do for now is to say most of time the markets are in consolidation. This is a range bound market and regardless of how price is moving within it, going side ways or making rising or falling flags, and every other formation people wish to call it......this is profit taking and positioning and those times of consolidation is where pro money are setting up for the next move. The content of my posts are all about what happens after this period of consolidation is no longer hidden. By the time we see the price action on our platforms pro money is already fully committed and the push has already been put in place. Once the break happens markets forces take over and price rises with new entrants and surprise surprise, hedge funds, mutual funds, banks and so on, until joe public gets in far too late. Conventional wisdom is wait for an established trend where there are higher highs and higher lows. Thats too late.

One final item I will mention while it is on my mind is the use of indicators and why I still see far too many traders trying to work with these tools of propaganda. Every indicator is 'some' twisted mathematical function of price, it has to be. If you are going to twist and manipulate price how do you ever expect to see what is happening?....there are only three components to every market and every financial instrument trade. Price, time and volume. Everything else is a complete fudge and provides zero information you need.

Price we can see, nothing surprising there. Time we can see, but the likes of the MT4 platform chops all contracts traded into equal time slices, this is a disadvantage because we cannot see how many contracts it took to fill that candle. Which brings me to volume. This shows how much activity there has been in the last candle, but again, it is of more importance to be able to see this where time is not skewing the activity. I am not sure if this has clicked with many, so here is another way to look at it.

If we had a candle that does not close based on time, but closes after say... x ticks. And we can adjust x to any value we wish. Now we can see how fast the market is moving and in what direction. Now take that info and plot it over a number of candles (not timed close candles). Tick charts help, but MT4 is useless for that. Also a hindering us is the lack of centeralised forex volume. The best you can hope to get is the volume from your broker. If your broker has a small number of clients, the volume will also be lower than a larger broker. Take it further and look for a paid data feed service from the CME. Its not cheap and a few grand a year wont go far.

If I take a guess that most people here want to stick to a freebie MT4 package and pull what they can from the market. You need to look at price movement in blocks of its ranges it makes as each candle in each time frame closes. This is akin to teaching your brain to see renko candles and point and figure charts. I believe there is renko candles for MT4 but you will loose subtle price action, such as wicks and tails. Take the block and compare it against price action. What you will eventually see is price takes up to 1hr of time and price action on most of the false moves. Within this time you watch for a change in direction after what looks like an obvious move. Pro money doesnt not want you along for the ride and so will pull the common sucker punch. Even if the move was not a false move you are still ok, because you wait for the pull back and again, watch for a continuation and where price action in the pull back is not making progress.

On higher time frame turns you may not get a pull back from some time, there is just far too much pro money after coming in which absorbs all other orders in such rapid action that a pull back cant happen. This is what happened in the chart I posted.

I note on most trades and analysis posted that there is a lack of candle stick explanations. All traders first port of call is learn what candle sticks tell you. I think I mentioned it before that a guy named Steve Nisson has a good book on candle sticks. He is one of the few I consider savvy in reading them. The names of the candle sticks and the formations they make is not important, but what is important is what it means at that point in time on every chart time frame. The markets are all fractals of each other and you can prove that quickly by seeing a bearish candle stick on a 4hr chart, but yet the same 4hr close has also got a 1min close candle chart where that candle is incredible bullish. Get that into your brain and its powerful information.

I have rambled on from a reply to Mel to some kind of lecture, sorry Mel:)

Anyways, hope some of you get something from it.

We always appreciate the lectures doc!

baltimore, I dont know Al Brooks or know anything about him. But given the prices he has on books and courses it makes me think I really ought to have a paypal button on my posts. But seriously, I find no reason why any professional trader has the need to sell books, courses, DVD's, mentoring etc. If a professional needs to do that, I would have to reason their own trading may not be making them enough money.

Many times every month I get requests to write books, make DVD videos, produce courses etc. But why?....I can make a lot more money trading.

One other common question I get in here is, why do I chose me tell people how I trade and not have my hand out. Well, its many reasons and one of the main reasons is the false information people get from books and courses and other websites where its clear to me there is a culture of keeping unsuccessful traders on the hook for buying yet more books and courses etc.

But if the info I give is really good, shouldnt I charge for it. I chose not to.

The best thing all traders can do is learn to read candles, learn how all time frames are connected, learn the signs of active pro money. It really is not complex, it has just been shown to you in a way that plays into the hands of pro money by keeping you out when you should be in, and ahaking you out where you were right, and getting you in as the move is ending.

People have short attention spans, and in todays world of over information and fast profits they forget about how markets work. One example before I retire for the evening where I have a date with a tall tasty blonde.......Carlsberg and BBQ:)

Gold. When the media pimped gold not many months ago it was on bad news. Oh the stock market is failing and the smart money is investing in Gold because it is a safe haven when even the currencies are falling and getting in now means you will be in before 2000 is hit and then off it will fly. The truth was a long way from that. Most trading platforms would not have given you the big picture even on the higher time frames, which is why I still keep old fashioned paper charts going back to the 1900's. Back in the 1970's gold hit 1800 bucks an ounce. What price did gold hit when it was being pimped up?....you guessed it, 1800 bucks. Then it collapsed and all the pro money helped by pushing it hard to give the illusion of higher profits. How stupid traders were even after the peak, the media again pimped that it was a pull back and had all the experts on shows to say it was a great buying opportunity to get back in for those who missed the move. More lies.

The great unwind has happened and a major cycle completed. it has taken decades for that to come and go, but how many day traders looked at the history?

Those eagle eyed among you will spot on higher time frames that ALL and I mean ALL traded instruments reach their peak cycles with great vigor. Thats where the media then come into play to get you into the trade. If you get a few days or even a couple of weeks with profits coming in, you are happy. Then you get the next pro money money which is them exiting their positions nice and slow so that they dont move the market against them too much and all retail traders are happy to take the pull backs cos thats what they see....its just a pull back.

One final item worth mentioning. Those indicators many traders like to use all work on trending markets perfectly all the time. Imagine that, and indicator that works perfectly in a trending market. But when in consolidation where pro money is loading/off loading they dont work and this is really where the chop from the indicators ALL fail.....ALL fail. I include trend lines in that statement, they too will fail and do no represent what is happening in the market because price is not a vector and its movement in how far it travels vertically in time is not dependent on time, it is dependent on activity and that can happen at any time pro money is active. Make sense?

thenew, when pro money want to stop and reverse the market it has to be done slowly. There is a huge amount of money that they have off load and then start the reverse. What happens is when prices reaches historic areas of interest, and in the example of eur/usd we got well into daily+ demand and this was where pro money will start their work.

As price is reaching this area of interest a few things has to happen, they want to get more of the herd selling. The best way to get any retail trader to sell is to push price hard and it can be seen it two large down candles on your chart. Note how the first candle had a pull back giving some comfort to early retail shorts where they would have added to their positions. Once the pull back was complete it was clear that more low cost long orders by pro money was required, so one final big push breaking all recent lows would have gotta the herd well and truly short. When there is what looks like apparent strength in the market on up or down candles at historic areas, it really represents the end of the move and weakness to follow on quickly.

If you look at the last large down candle note how the next candle is bullish and closes on its highs, the next candle closes inside the previous showing no intent to push lower. The price action that follows the end of any move can be very difficult to read because there is no specific pattern pro money use. The whole concept for them is to allow the period of consolidation be a hiding place for the new direction they wish to take and get most of the orders into the market before everyone else. If they succeed what happens is a bullish break which takes out the top of the last pull back on the way down.

Once that part is completed all other pro money traders know the short side is over, and they may or may not have missed the bearish orders being absorbed within the consolidation and long orders being filtered in. If you think logically about all of this is makes sense. If a pull back or period of consolidation is the place where the market will reverse, there cannot be a significant break of the lowest low within that area, a spike is fine as it brings it the cheapest long orders they can get.

But if more spikes and more fast tests below for more shorts happen, the pro bulls risk pro bears seeing this and thinking, there are more willing takers for my shorts so we will push hard. It is the most difficult time for pro money because they can loose a lot of money if their test and false break go too far or happen too often. They need to soak up all sellers and the candle will then contract and look very small and most retail traders cannot see what is going on. All of this is deliberate and keeps you out, this is the idea, you must be out of the market when pro money is loading up. If you are in, there will shake you out soon after, or at least try. But they cant shake too hard in case they break recent lows with too much vigor.

One firm of pro money will not know what other firms are doing and if more than one were to attempt a shake out around the same time, price will move quickly because suddenly a lot of money comes into the market. Its a real balancing act.

Once I see pull backs or consolidation happening where price is in a tight range, I will drop down to the 1min chart. If I had tick charts I would choose a low value tick. I want to see who is taking most of the action within the small range. In the case of the euro reverse last week, I will look for buying opportunities off the bottom of the range and filter in longs as I see them come up, I take everyone I see until I am fully committed to the capital I wish to risk. The purpose of scaling in like this means my risk in lower in case there is a sudden strong movement that goes into my stop. If I were fully committed on the first position and a sudden move happened I would loose more. Let me give an example, lets say I have a small account of 3 grand and I wont trade more than half a standard lot. I take each trade with a.1 position size and continue placing trades as I see entries. Once I reach five.1 lot trades I wont place anymore. Each position now has a hard stop below price at a point count suitable for the risk I wish to accept.

On my posted trade they were dozens on entries over a 1min chart. There are other ways to place the trade(s) but it is up to the individual trader to decide what they wish to do. My way is not the be and end all, it is just how I approach it so please dont take it as the only way.

It is not practical to take trades of the 15min chart if you want entries like mine, you miss the entire break which tends to be spectacular when higher time frames are unwound and reversed. But when markets are trending taking 5min and 15min chart entries is fine.

Once pro money is committed in their chosen direction and they are loaded up, price is given one final push out of consolidation where it break in grand style. This is the only time pro money will push price, once they are all in, or at least most of them, price will come back for a test in the form of a pull back somewhere in the future. When that happens others who were not in at the beginning will wait for the pull back to slow and start placing orders. As more orders come in price will again rise and break the new high, then we see the hedge funds, mutual funds, banks come in. Further on when there is a clear sign of a market that is trending we get the herd come in because they can see the teaching of the books was correct because there is a clear trend and the indicator crew follow soon after. At this point in time we are approaching the end of the main move. We know it will be the end because we will see what look like very strong candle with long bodies and price pushing hard. the media will be pimping this to the moon and more retail money coming in. It is vital pro money get you long here because they will be the ones selling to you, as you want to desperately get in on the action. Pro money is first in and first out. The market move ends as it began with false promise of more upside and the strings inside peoples minds get pulled in every direction to get you in, or keep you in just that little bit longer. Fools gold.

The main disadvantage we have is not being able to see real order flow. We want actual numbers on how many buyers and sellers are coming into the market. Forex has no central exchange and its not possible to get that data from your broker because they do not represent the full picture of what is going on, only what is going on within their own clients. This is why we spend so much time and effort reading the signs of pro money activity in the tracks they leave in closed candles on all time frames. There is one change in the market over past few years that make low time frame candle reading more difficult, automated trading. Those pesky machines effect how price reacts and give more spikes than we would expect from years back if we were looking at the same...... say 15min chart.

A rather long answer and going in places that came to mind as I typed this. But I hope it answered your question and gave you some insight.

Taking entries off the 1min chart when the market is consolidating will blow accounts faster than any other method if you have never spent a lot of time doing it. In comparison, taking entries on pullbacks is a much easier place to start.

The candles you high lighted all look fine to me, but in hind sight all entries are. The question is, can you see them in real time as the market marches onward? Try marking candles on the chart when the market reopens and do it for an entire week, then see how many were correct. It can be a humbling exercise.

I take 1min entries around these reversal areas because its the fastest data I can get on the platform. it is not as good as I would like, but there is little else to use unless I go back into futures.

Given the pair has now reversed, all historic supply areas are weaker and with little sellers remaining. This allows price to rise easier than if these areas were not tested when price was on the way down. The tests tend to be made up of spikes, pullbacks in the many forms they bring, and slow meandering price action, each has a story to tell.

There are people and businesses on the internet selling courses based upon candle sticks that have long wicks and tails. If you fall into the trap of only looking for those you wont be as successful as you could be. Pro money knows that hiding their true intentions until the last possible moment before the market moves is important. That means candles with long wicks or tails wont always show the move. Safer entries for newer traders and for those who have been at this for some time but have yet to make good money out it are better to wait for the break to happen, pull back and then enter when the direction has been chosen by pro money and where there is an obvious target they are gunning for. But if you miss the first pull back you might, just might get a second. Miss the second and its highly unlikely there will be another good slice of the action left, other than the pro money emotionally driven final push to get you in as they are off loading.

Try marking candles on the chart when the market reopens and do it for an entire week, then see how many were correct. It can be a humbling exercise.

It will take time and patience to become good at trading. The money is made in trends, if you are not in the trend before the main move begins, you must wait for it to pull back and then enter. When the market is taking off the fast moves and price moving swiftly away will tug most peoples emotional strings and then they chase it. That is the worst thing you can do. Having the patience to wait for it to come back to cheaper prices and where the pro's are making adjustments to their orders is the only place you can enter with low risk.

When I look for the next move I have many hours watching consolidation for signs of activity. if I miss where pro money is loading up, I will wait for the break to stop, reverse and find where positions are being added to and I will then get in.

You can be assured that there will always be some place you can get in. Pro money can not always get all their positions on before the break, and this is why we see pull backs. But in periods of long consolidation most pro money can get all their positions in place and the longer this consolidation goes on, the more powerful and violent the move out will be.

Be fully aware of what is happening on all time frames as each subsequent time frame candle closes. And only ever take decisions on closed candles. Around major S/R is where you can expect to get the best profit from a trade. I prefer to take the longer term moves rather than pull 15 or 20 points at a time. My logic like all my trading is simple, why risk the same spread, but risk higher pull backs when trading lower time frames, when I can place the same size lot on higher time frame S/R knowing if the area is to hold, pro money will defend the low or high of the area, depending on it begin a bullish or bearish new move. If the major S/R will hold there will be a point of pain that the pros will not want hit and will absorb all attempts to push beyond it. Only deep pockets can go so far and then the market moves when more buyers or sellers out weight the other.
